about: Authored query pairs on Northwind for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the Northwind data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Orders.CustomerID references Customers' key: an order joins one customer exactly when CustomerID is not NULL
pairs.left: SELECT o.OrderID FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID FROM Orders WHERE CustomerID IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Orders.CustomerID may be NULL: such an order joins no customer
pairs.left: SELECT o.OrderID FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID FROM Orders

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key an order may name a customer that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT o.OrderID FROM Orders AS o JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID FROM Orders WHERE CustomerID IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: (OrderID, ProductID) is the key of Order Details
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT OrderID, ProductID, Quantity FROM `Order Details`
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID, ProductID, Quantity FROM `Order Details`

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: one order holds several lines of the same quantity
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT OrderID, Quantity FROM `Order Details`
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID, Quantity FROM `Order Details`

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the key a line may appear twice
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT OrderID, ProductID, Quantity FROM `Order Details`
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID, ProductID, Quantity FROM `Order Details`

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Order Details.OrderID is NOT NULL and references Orders' key
pairs.left: SELECT od.OrderID, od.ProductID FROM `Order Details` AS od JOIN Orders AS o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID, ProductID FROM `Order Details`

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the join condition also filters on the product, so lines of discontinued products drop out
pairs.left: SELECT od.OrderID, od.ProductID FROM `Order Details` AS od JOIN Products AS p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID AND p.Discontinued = 0
pairs.right: SELECT OrderID, ProductID FROM `Order Details`

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the LEFT JOIN to the manager matches at most one employee (EmployeeID is the key) and reads nothing from it
pairs.left: SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.LastName FROM Employees AS e LEFT JOIN Employees AS m ON m.EmployeeID = e.ReportsTo
pairs.right: SELECT EmployeeID, LastName FROM Employees

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: joining the employees who report to e repeats a manager once per report
pairs.left: SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.LastName FROM Employees AS e LEFT JOIN Employees AS m ON m.ReportsTo = e.EmployeeID
pairs.right: SELECT EmployeeID, LastName FROM Employees

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Suppliers.Region holds NULLs, so NOT IN returns no row
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerID FROM Customers WHERE Region NOT IN (SELECT Region FROM Suppliers)
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID FROM Customers AS c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Suppliers AS s WHERE s.Region = c.Region)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both CustomerID columns are NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerID FROM Customers WHERE CustomerID NOT IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM CustomerCustomerDemo)
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID FROM Customers AS c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM CustomerCustomerDemo AS d WHERE d.CustomerID = c.CustomerID)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: CategoryID is Categories' key, so the join matches at most one category and repeats no product
pairs.left: SELECT p.ProductName FROM Products AS p WHERE p.CategoryID IN (SELECT CategoryID FROM Categories WHERE CategoryName = 'Seafood')
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductName FROM Products AS p JOIN Categories AS c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE c.CategoryName = 'Seafood'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: many suppliers share a country, so the join repeats customers
pairs.left: SELECT c.CompanyName FROM Customers AS c WHERE c.Country IN (SELECT Country FROM Suppliers)
pairs.right: SELECT c.CompanyName FROM Customers AS c JOIN Suppliers AS s ON s.Country = c.Country

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: OrderID is the key and NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT OrderID) FROM Orders
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: customers place several orders
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) FROM Orders
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the grouping column can run before the grouping
pairs.left: SELECT * FROM (SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Products GROUP BY CategoryID) WHERE CategoryID = 1
pairs.right: SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Products WHERE CategoryID = 1 GROUP BY CategoryID

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a category whose products are all discontinued is missing on the left and counted 0 on the right
pairs.left: SELECT CategoryID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = 0 GROUP BY CategoryID
pairs.right: SELECT CategoryID, COUNTIF(Discontinued = 0) AS n FROM Products GROUP BY CategoryID

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: o.EmployeeID = 5 rejects the NULL-extended rows of the LEFT JOIN
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerID, o.OrderID FROM Customers AS c LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.EmployeeID = 5
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID, o.OrderID FROM Customers AS c JOIN Orders AS o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.EmployeeID = 5

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: two customers have no order; IS NULL keeps their NULL-extended rows
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerID, o.OrderID FROM Customers AS c LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.EmployeeID = 5 OR o.EmployeeID IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID, o.OrderID FROM Customers AS c JOIN Orders AS o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.EmployeeID = 5 OR o.EmployeeID IS NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the union of a query with itself, without duplicates, is its distinct rows
pairs.left: SELECT Country FROM Customers UNION DISTINCT SELECT Country FROM Customers
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT Country FROM Customers

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Customers.CustomerID is NOT NULL, so INTERSECT's NULL matching never applies
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerID FROM Customers INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT c.CustomerID FROM Customers AS c WHERE c.CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: INTERSECT matches a NULL city with a NULL city; IN does not
pairs.left: SELECT City FROM Customers INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT City FROM Employees
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT c.City FROM Customers AS c WHERE c.City IN (SELECT City FROM Employees)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Territories.RegionID is NOT NULL and references Region's key
pairs.left: SELECT t.TerritoryID FROM Territories AS t JOIN Region AS r ON r.RegionID = t.RegionID
pairs.right: SELECT TerritoryID FROM Territories

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: once RegionID may be NULL, such a territory joins no region
pairs.left: SELECT t.TerritoryID FROM Territories AS t JOIN Region AS r ON r.RegionID = t.RegionID
pairs.right: SELECT TerritoryID FROM Territories
